SMTO-EXE-0012 — The Python code for this step wasn't in the required form

GUID: 2881b245-d1d7-4816-a1de-4c467e3d7954
Slug: python-entrypoint-required
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO wrote a small Python program for this step, but it wasn't laid out the way SMTO requires, so it was refused. No Python ran and nothing changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Watch the task for a moment. SMTO usually rewrites the code and tries the step again on its own. The refusal is sent back to SMTO's model with what to change, and since no Python ran, a corrected try is safe.
  2. If it keeps failing, open Settings › Agent behavior › Advanced and make sure Automatic Python correction is turned on. When it's on, SMTO fixes this layout mistake by itself before checking the code.
  3. Then start a new task with the same request. A task keeps the setting it started with, so only a new task picks up the change.

What success looks like

  • The Python step runs and shows its result in the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. If you wrote the code yourself, put all of it, including imports, inside a function named main(inputs), or transform(inputs) for data transforms.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Python source validation rejected the code before launch because it lacks the required top-level main(inputs) or transform(inputs) function as the first definition, with imports and executable statements inside it.

What this means

  • Python source validation did not find the required main or transform function in the position required by the active schema checks. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Python source validation did not find the required main or transform function in the position required by the active schema checks.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare source structure with the advertised main(inputs) or transform(inputs) entrypoint and the effective validation policy.

How to fix it

  • Make the code start with def main(inputs): (python_action) or def transform(inputs): (python_transform), with imports and all executable statements inside it and no decorators or annotations. Enable python_entrypoint_auto_correction_enabled (Settings › Agent behavior › Advanced › Automatic Python correction; applies to new tasks) to let the runtime wrap eligible source without a model call.
  • Correct source to the advertised entrypoint. Supported deterministic auto-correction may wrap eligible source when enabled; no model call is needed to add that wrapper.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended source passes entrypoint validation without changing its requested behavior.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
